newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine coconut oil prices seen remaining high.
newsitem.headline: Philippine coconut oil prices seen remaining high.

text.p: Philippine coconut oil prices are expected to remain at current high prices due to tight supply as a result of delayed copra harvests, traders said on Wednesday.
"The tightness in supply has spawned hand-to-mouth buyers," said one dealer.

Traders said copra supply from the southern island of Mindanao, which accounts for 30 to 35 percent of Philippine supply, dwindled as persistent rains last month delayed harvests in major coconut growing areas.
"Hopefully, copra supply in Mindanao would stabilise by the end of the month with improved weather," said another dealer.

Philippine coconut oil exports dropped to an average of 66,823 tonnes per month in the first nine months of the year against 113,940 in the same period last year, preliminary data from the trade group United Coconut Associations of the Philippines (UCAP) said.

"Although the bulk of the supply deficit is due to the onslaught of typhoons starting last year and up to this year, increasing local demand for coconut oil and heightened demand from the oleochemicals sector are putting pressure on the supply side," said one trader.
The high cost of coconut oil has driven some buyers to shift to the cheaper palm oil. "At present, a tonne of palm oil is $150 to $200 cheaper than its coconut oil equivalent," said one dealer.
"Coconut oil prices are expected to soften only if supply becomes more fluid and this may happen only in 1997 when the farmers would have recovered from the onslaught of the typhoons," a dealer said.
Coconut oil prices are expected to hit a high of $730 per tonne CIF and a low of $705 for forward months, traders said.
UCAP said sellers' offered coconut oil at $742.50 per tonne CIF for September/October and an average of $731.25 for November December on Wednesday.
UCAP said buyers quoted prices at an average $733.75 per tonne CIF for September/October and $722.5 for October/November delivery.
"I do not see anything spectacular that would rock the boat, so prices will likely remain at this level in the short term," one dealer said.
